resources.name: learning-mtls
resources.description:
Mutual-TLS demo: service-consumer (:9443, one-way TLS) calls service-producer (:8443, client-auth=need) with its client certificate.

Certificates are not part of an Insomnia import. Set them once via the collection sidebar → **Certificates**:

1. **Add CA Certificate** → `<repo>/insomnia-certs/ca.crt` (root README → 18.2) — do this before sending any request
2. **Add Client Certificate** → Host `localhost:8443`, PFX or PKCS12 `<repo>/service-consumer/src/main/resources/ssl/service-consumer-keystore.p12`, Passphrase `changeit`
3. **Add Client Certificate** → Host `127.0.0.1:8443`, PFX or PKCS12 `<repo>/service-producer/src/test/resources/ssl/service-unknown-keystore.p12`, Passphrase `changeit`

resources.name: service-consumer — one-way TLS (localhost:9443)
resources.description: No client certificate needed; only the CA certificate. For each request the consumer calls service-producer over mTLS, presenting its own client certificate.

resources.name: GET — Hello via producer (fr)
resources.description: Expected: `200`. `upstream.callerCn` = `service-consumer` is the CN the producer read from the consumer's client certificate — proof that mTLS happened.

resources.name: GET — Hello, unknown language (404)
resources.description: Expected: `404` `application/problem+json` — `Greeting not found upstream` (the producer's 404 passed through).

resources.name: GET — Consumer Info
resources.description: `app.downstream` shows the producer URL the consumer calls.

resources.name: service-producer — mTLS as service-consumer (localhost:8443)
resources.description: Uses the client certificate configured for host `localhost:8443`: `service-consumer-keystore.p12`, CN `service-consumer`, which is allow-listed.

resources.name: service-producer — mTLS as service-unknown (127.0.0.1:8443)
resources.description: Uses the client certificate configured for host `127.0.0.1:8443`: `service-unknown-keystore.p12`, CN `service-unknown`. The TLS handshake succeeds (same CA), then the CN allow-list rejects the caller. Same producer as `localhost:8443` — its certificate is valid for both names (SAN).

resources.name: GET — Greeting (403 Forbidden)
resources.description: Expected: `403` — Spring Boot's default error JSON (not a problem detail), because `ClientCertificateFilter` rejects the request before Spring MVC.

resources.name: GET — Producer Health (200, CN check exempt)
resources.description: Expected: `200` — `/actuator/health` skips the CN allow-list; the TLS layer still requires a CA-signed client certificate.

resources.name: GET — Producer Info (403)
resources.description: Expected: `403` — unlike health, `/actuator/info` goes through the CN allow-list.

resources.name: service-producer — no client certificate (handshake failure)
resources.description: First disable the `localhost:8443` client certificate (sidebar → Certificates), then send. Re-enable it afterwards.

resources.name: GET — Greeting without client cert (TLS alert)
resources.description: Expected: no HTTP response. Tomcat (`client-auth: need`) aborts the handshake with TLS alert 116 `certificate_required`; Insomnia reports curl error 56, `Failure when receiving data from the peer`.
